summary: Three current authority boundaries with limitations stated beside them. Kit is a source-checkout BYOP preview, not a release artifact. Its implemented vault encrypts the complete provider list and active id in ~/.hoplight/kit-vault.json rather than splitting metadata and secrets. Windows uses CurrentUser DPAPI end to end; a portable scrypt plus AES-256-GCM passphrase backend is unit-proven but the settings flow does not yet collect or pass a passphrase on macOS or Linux. Environment-variable providers remain cross-platform and unpersisted. Vault writes use temp plus rename and best-effort mode 0600 but no fsync; valid sealed envelopes fail loudly on backend or authentication errors, while malformed outer JSON or an invalid envelope is currently treated as no vault; there is no recovery, export, backend migration, or rotation flow. Provider egress rejects unknown or unkeyed providers and initial request URLs outside the one fixed or configured host; redirects are runtime-managed rather than hop-validated. Credentials go only as provider authentication, while conversation and tool observations are the model payload; privacy receipts retain provider and token counts, not bodies or keys. The Studio server binds loopback, mints a per-launch bearer, checks Host on every API method, rejects cross-site reads, requires Origin plus token for POST and PATCH, and caps bodies. Ordinary assets are ungated, but the ungated index HTML also contains the bearer and relies on loopback reachability rather than bearer authentication for confidentiality. Its second sandbox listener allowlists worker assets and withholds the bearer; Bun HTTP behavior is proven, packaged WebView separation remains unmeasured, and same-origin fallback is degraded.

sections.title: Kit provider vault (shipping source preview)
sections.summary: Current Kit BYOP boundary, not the obsolete packages/ai design. Offline import edit inspect validate convert and deterministic analysis need no key. Provider-backed turns use a discovered built-in or OpenAI-compatible endpoint; unknown providers and keyed providers without keys fail before request. Kit runs from a source checkout with bun run kit. The private package exposes that entry, but current GitHub Releases contain Hoplight.exe and hoplight CLI binaries only. The implemented vault, its three platform backends including the local key file fallback that keeps non-Windows machines encrypted rather than blocked, host-locked egress, and explicit recovery gaps are shipping source-preview behavior.

children.title: What the vault seals
children.summary: Saved providers live in ~/.hoplight/kit-vault.json or HOPLIGHT_HOME. Current code does not split public metadata from secret state: it encrypts the complete Vault object, including every ProviderConfig API key base URL headers options and label plus activeId. Disk holds only version backend and opaque payload; round-trip coverage proves neither key nor provider name appears in plaintext. The decrypted vault is cached in process memory. Writes seal a temporary sibling, attempt mode 0600, then rename over the vault, protecting the prior file from a partial write but without fsync of file or directory.

children.title: Backends and present platform boundary
children.summary: The registry prefers Windows DPAPI, then the local key file, then the master passphrase. Opening follows the backend tag on the blob and never silently falls back. DPAPI pipes base64 plaintext through hidden noninteractive PowerShell, binding recovery to the same Windows user. The local key file is the universal fallback where no OS-native backend runs: a generated 256-bit key in a versioned 104-byte blob with HMAC integrity and owner-only mode, encrypting the vault with AES-256-GCM. It is re-read per operation, never cached, so a file removed underneath a running Kit is noticed. It is deliberately weaker and labeled so, since its key sits beside the vault. macOS Keychain and Linux Secret Service are unimplemented. Passphrase reports unavailable, never auto-selected.
topics: weaker than DPAPI and labeled so

children.title: Provider egress boundary
children.summary: All provider spokes receive guarded fetch. Built-in spokes fix a host; custom and local spokes derive one host from configured baseURL. Unknown providers, missing required keys, and request URLs outside that host fail before network; model discovery uses the same gate. Credentials necessarily travel to the configured endpoint as authentication but are not inserted in conversations tools transcripts canonical entities or exports. The model receives conversation plus tool and docs observations needed for the request. Privacy records provider and token counts only. The current gate validates the initial request URL but delegates redirects to runtime and does not revalidate each hop.

children.title: Recovery limitations
children.summary: Valid sealed envelopes fail loudly on an unknown backend, DPAPI failure, wrong passphrase, or GCM authentication failure, and DPAPI binds the blob to the Windows user. There is no vault export, recovery key, backend migration, or credential rotation flow. One documented exception: a structurally invalid local key file already holds an unrecoverable key, so failing closed protects nothing while trapping the user. Kit sets the damaged file and the unopenable vault aside under dated names, writes a fresh key, and returns an empty vault with a notice naming both paths; neither is deleted. I/O failures may succeed on retry and are surfaced, not treated as damage. Tampered ciphertext under a healthy key still throws untouched.

sections.title: The loopback server (shipping)
sections.summary: Shipping code with automated Bun tests. The default visual app binds 127.0.0.1 only, and uploaded scripts remain data. A random per-launch bearer is injected into index HTML for trusted apiFetch and never handed to the sandbox. The api gate runs before every api handler, checks Host on every method, refuses cross-site GET and HEAD, and requires Origin plus token for POST and PATCH. JavaScript wasm CSS and icons are non-secret ungated assets. Index HTML is also ungated but contains the bearer, so its confidentiality relies on loopback reachability; any client that reaches the listener can read it. Reads remain weaker than mutations. Body caps are 64MB inspect and 32MB JSON.

children.title: The per-launch bearer
children.summary: A fresh bearer is minted once per launch as randomBytes(32).toString base64url in createSecurityContext marked never log or persist. injectSessionMeta puts it into served index HTML as an escaped meta name vaude-session which trusted apiFetch reads for API authentication. The token is never handed to the sandbox origin. The index document itself is not bearer-gated, so the default listener's loopback bind limits which machines can fetch it; any local client that reaches the listener can read the bearer.

children.title: The /api/* gate
children.summary: Every api route runs through checkApiRequest before its handler. JavaScript wasm CSS and icons are non-secret and ungated. Index HTML is also ungated but is not non-secret: createHandler injects the bearer before serving it, so confidentiality relies on the default loopback bind and any client reaching the listener can read it. The api gate returns 503 before security context completion, checks Host on every method, and rejects attacker hostnames resolved to loopback. GET and HEAD carry no token but reject Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site. POST and PATCH require a loopback-equivalent non-null Origin and a timingSafeEqual token. Other methods return 405.

children.title: What the gate does not do
children.summary: Stated plainly because overclaiming would be a defect. localhost and ::1 on the correct port are accepted not rejected; only wrong port or foreign hostname fails closed. All three loopback spellings resolve to the same bound interface so rejecting localhost would paper-cut bookmarks while protecting nothing; the gate stops attacker hostnames not loopback aliases. GET and HEAD are not token-gated: a header-less client curl or older browser with no Sec-Fetch-Site passes the read gate. The read gate is deliberately weaker than the mutation gate. Reads that expose entity data rely on the loopback bind and cross-site refusal not on the bearer.

children.title: Body caps
children.summary: Request bodies stream with a hard byte cap and 413 on overflow: INSPECT_BODY_MAX 64MB JSON_BODY_MAX 32MB. readBodyCapped checks Content-Length early when present and enforces a running total as it reads so a lying or absent length header still cannot exceed the cap. Same fail-closed posture the upload adapters use against zip bombs.

sections.title: The sandbox origin (shipping code, packaged proof BLOCKED)
sections.summary: Untrusted Lua from the Risu Test Bench runs in a Worker from a second loopback listener on an ephemeral port, a distinct origin from UI and api. Defense-in-depth: same-origin Worker is a killable thread not an origin boundary so a future WebView or bundler bug would widen blast radius if same-origin. Fails closed by construction: serves only sandbox worker.js regex-worker.js and glue.wasm; every other path 404 with locked CSP; no api no index HTML no session token no traversal. CORS limited to exact UI origin plus loopback aliases so only trusted UI constructs the cross-origin module Worker. API token is never injected into anything this host serves. What is proven and what is not: allowlist CORS value-only wire API denial and token absence proven at Bun HTTP layer; packaged WebView2 isolation not measured; Plan 017 BLOCKED; do not claim fully isolated; same-origin fallback degraded not claimed isolated.

children.title: What is proven, and what is not
children.summary: Scaffolding additive to token Plan 005 and resource quotas Plan 016 not a replacement. Proven: allowlist CORS value-only wire API denial and token absence by Bun HTTP and handler tests. Not measured: packaged WebView2 origin isolation, whether WebView collapses two loopback authorities, crossOriginIsolated and storage separation, and credentialed API fetch from sandbox origin; Plan 017 BLOCKED until a WebView2 smoke matrix records those. Do not call the sandbox fully isolated sandboxed or exploit-proof. Until the matrix is green it is defense-in-depth with tested HTTP behavior and unmeasured in-WebView separation. Sandbox bind failure falls back to same-origin Worker explicitly degraded and not claimed isolated.
